items.basis: The proposed mechanism fails to account for the fundamental electrochemical incompatibility between nickel/cobalt catalysts and the lead-acid system, as these metals promote oxygen evolution rather than hydrogen evolution in acidic environments, contradicting the core HER claim.

The 2.27 V per cell boundary condition creates a thermodynamically unstable environment where the proposed additives would accelerate rather than reduce corrosion, as evidenced by [doi:10.1109/intlec.1995.498976] which shows grid corrosion rates increase exponentially above 2.25V.

The candidate's own evidence bundle contradicts the claimed effect, as [doi:10.1109/bcaa.2000.838406] demonstrates that improved charge algorithms reduce corrosion more effectively than metallic additives, making the proposed approach redundant at best.

The claimed 50% reduction in cross-section reduction rate is unsupported by any data in the evidence bundle, while [doi:10.1016/s0378-7753(98)00028-7] shows that existing designs already achieve 10+ year lifespaces without such additives.

The 66:17:17 ppm ratio cannot be uniformly distributed in a lead alloy casting due to significant differences in melting points and densities between lead and the additives, creating localized hotspots that would accelerate rather than inhibit corrosion.

The testable prediction fails to specify measurement methodology, sampling points, or time intervals for cross-section evaluation, allowing for selective reporting that could mask the actual lack of improvement over baseline.
